newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - June 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ivory Coast - June 20.

text.p: These are significant items in the Ivorian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these items and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Classes resume at Cocody University in Ivory Coast's commercial capital Abidjan despite attacks by students who want to prolong a boycott of classes.

- Turnover of insurers CICA-RE (La Compagnie Commune de Reassurance des 12 etats African Francophone de la zone franc) rose 10.68 percent in 1996 financial year, thanks to restructuring and other reforms, its chairman says.

- Veteran opposition leader Laurent Gbagbo says in an interview that his Ivorian Popular Front has taken note of President Henri Konan Bedie's stated desire to form a broad-based government but says this is not the focus of debate within the party; says that in any case the real issue is what such a government will do

- Security forces deploy on Cocody University campus after clashes between students for and against a resumption of classes in dispute over examinations, latest in string of grievances - Ivory Coast's arbitration court CACI will start operating in July, offering the business world an alternative way of settling disputes, its secretary general Narcisse Aka says; businessmen and women and lawyers attend seminar on the workings of the court.
